question: The technique of watering plants by making use of narrow tubes which deliver water directly at the base of the plant is called ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**drip irrigation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drip irrigation **is a technique where water is delivered directly to the **root zone of plants** through a network of** tubes or pipes** with small holes or emitters.
 
• This method is highly efficient as it r**educes water loss** due to evaporation, runoff, or deep percolation.
 
• Drip irrigation also helps in** reducing weed growth, soil erosion, and disease incidence.**
 
• This technique can be used for various crops, including **vegetables, fruits, flowers, and trees.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sprinkler irrigation** is a method where water is distributed through **sprinklers** that spray water over the crops.

 
 
• This method is suitable for** larger areas,** but it can lead to** water wastage **due to wind drift and evaporation. 
 
 
 
• **Canal irrigation** is a traditional method where water is supplied to crops through** canals or ditches**.
 
 
• This method is suitable for areas with **abundant water resources**, but it can lead to **waterlogging and soil salinization.**
 
 
 
• **Surface irrigation** is a method where water is applied to the soil surface and allowed to **infiltrate into the root zone.**
 
 
• This method is suitable for crops that can** tolerate wet conditions, **but it can lead to **uneven distribution of water** and nutrient leaching.
